chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha' from Fadl Abu al-Abbas who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Is the man more entitled to his child or the woman? He said: No, but the man. However, if the woman says to her husband (the one who divorced her): I will breastfeed my son for the same amount you would pay whoever else you find to breastfeed him, then she is more entitled to him.

key_terms.بِمِثْلِ مَا: For the same amount / equivalent to

ai.seo_question: Who has primary custody of the child after divorce in Shia jurisprudence, and what is the exception?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), clarifying that while paternal custody is the default principle in Shia jurisprudence, it is contingent upon the mother's ability and willingness to provide breastfeeding. This exception highlights the practical consideration of the child's immediate welfare, establishing that the mother's right to custody is superior if she assumes the nursing role for equivalent compensation, thereby balancing paternal authority with maternal care. This hadith serves as a foundational text for the legal mechanism of *radāʿ* (breastfeeding) influencing custody rights in classical Shia fiqh.
